doctor.env_inherited: IssueRelay did not set PATH or a proxy: the executors get the environment IssueRelay was started with.
doctor.env_why: Apps started from the Dock, Finder or at login get only a minimal PATH, and Claude Code reads proxy settings only from environment variables, not from the system proxy. So IssueRelay reads PATH and the proxy variables from your login shell or the system settings and passes them to the executors.

help.description: When IssueRelay takes an issue on, how an issue moves, how to write one, and what to do when something does not work.
help.defaults_note: Showing the default names: the settings could not be read.
help.trigger_intro: IssueRelay works on an issue by itself only when all four of these hold:

conditions.assigned: The issue is assigned to you
conditions.label: It has the {{label}} label
conditions.bound: Its project is bound to a local folder and the executor is ready

help.trigger_note: Monitoring must not be paused either. The Issues page says why an issue was not picked up.
help.flow_text: You put an issue in {{todo}}. When it starts, the AI sets {{in_progress}}, and {{in_testing}} once its work is on the test branch. You look at the result and mark the issue done in the panel, which sets {{done}} in Linear: the only change IssueRelay makes in Linear.
help.flow_steps: The statuses of an issue in Linear
help.states_title: What the statuses in the panel mean

state_meaning.waiting_binding: The issue meets the conditions, but its project is not bound to a folder or its executor is not ready. It goes on once that is mended.
state_meaning.queued: It waits for its folder to be free or for a place among the runs allowed at the same time.
state_meaning.running: The executor is working on it.
state_meaning.awaiting_acceptance: The run ended well and the issue is in testing. Mark it done in the panel when you accept it.
state_meaning.needs_info: The AI found the issue unclear, asked on the issue and took the label off. Add the details and label it again.
state_meaning.failed: The run ended with an error, ran too long or went quiet, or the issue did not reach testing. Read the log and run it again.

help.example_intro: The clearer an issue, the better the result. Say what should happen, where, and how to tell it worked.

example.good_label: A request the AI can finish
example.good_title: Add a /health endpoint that returns the app version
example.good_body: GET /health answers with status 200 and the version from package.json as JSON, for example version 1.4.2. Cover it with a test and leave the other routes alone. Push to the test branch.
example.vague_label: A request the AI will ask about
example.vague_note: The AI cannot tell what to measure or what is fast enough, so it asks on the issue, sets the status back to {{todo}} and removes the label. Add the details and label it again.

help.lean_body: A lean run loads only Linear's MCP server and the repository's own rules and settings: not your other MCP servers, plugins, hooks, auto memory or user-level CLAUDE.md. Codex still reads ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, and the repository's .codex/ configuration does not apply. Bindings run lean unless you turn it off; personal-settings bindings and a binding of your home folder always use your whole setup.
help.lean_off: Turn it off for a binding that needs other MCP servers, the repository's .codex/ configuration, deny rules from your user settings, or a custom model provider.
help.lean_effort: Lean runs do not read the reasoning effort from your own settings: set a default reasoning effort in Settings, or one for each binding.

faq.not_picked_q: Why was my issue not picked up?
faq.not_picked_a: The Issues page says why for each issue. Usually the issue lacks the {{label}} label or is not in {{todo}}, its project has no binding, or its executor is not ready (see Environment). Monitoring must not be paused. An issue whose last run has ended is started again only after it changes in Linear, or when you choose Run again.
faq.permission_q: What do the three permission levels mean?
faq.permission_a: The level decides how much the AI may do without asking. It is set for each binding, or for all bindings in Settings.
faq.proxy_q: What if I need a proxy?
faq.proxy_a: Claude Code does not read the system proxy, only environment variables such as HTTPS_PROXY. IssueRelay reads them from your login shell or the system settings and passes them to the executors. Set them in your shell profile, restart IssueRelay, and look at the Environment page to see what was found; passwords are masked there.
faq.mcp_q: How can Claude Code or Codex use IssueRelay's MCP control server?
faq.mcp_a: In Settings, register the MCP control server with Claude Code or Codex. It is registered for your user, so unattended runs that are not lean load it too (lean runs load only Linear). Its tools let the AI see the status, list runs, pause and resume monitoring and check now; it cannot mark an issue done or run it again.
faq.logs_a: Open a run on the Runs page: the Raw log tab shows its log, and Copy all copies it. The files are in the logs folder inside IssueRelay's data folder (macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/com.sunkailun.issuerelay, Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\com.sunkailun.issuerelay). The program's own log, app.<date>.log, is there too.

description.language: The panel, the tray menu and the notifications use it. You can change it later in Settings.
description.linear: IssueRelay reads your issues through your Linear account. Marking an issue done in the panel is the only change it makes there. You authorize it in your browser.
description.workspace: IssueRelay needs the {{label}} label, and the statuses it moves an issue through, in your Linear workspace. It does not create them for you.
description.executors: IssueRelay hands each issue to Claude Code or Codex. At least one of them has to be installed, logged in and connected to Linear.
description.binding: Tell IssueRelay which folder on this computer belongs to a Linear project. Bindings can be added, edited and removed later on the Bindings page.
description.finish: What an issue needs before IssueRelay takes it on, and how it moves from there.

onboarding.no_executor: Install and log in to Claude Code or Codex first
onboarding.no_executor_hint: Follow what each card says below, then check again.
onboarding.no_binding_note: No project is bound yet, so IssueRelay will not take on any issue. Bind one on the Bindings page when you are ready.
onboarding.control_server_note: In Settings you can let Claude Code and Codex use IssueRelay's MCP control server. It is registered for your user, so unattended runs that are not lean load it too, and its tools can pause monitoring.
